"Create a complete mobile 3D puzzle adventure game called THE LAST FOLD.

CORE CONCEPT:
The entire game world is made of paper. The player controls a small character who must reach the exit of each level by physically folding the world using touchscreen gestures.

MAIN GAME MECHANICS:

- Swipe across the screen to create a fold line.
- Drag one side of the paper world over the other.
- Objects, platforms, enemies and characters move together with the folded paper.
- Overlapping surfaces can create bridges, shortcuts and new paths.
- Some objects can only be reached by flipping or folding the world.
- Incorrect folds can create obstacles or trap the player.

GAMEPLAY:

- Third-person isometric 3D camera.
- Smooth touchscreen controls.
- 100 progressively challenging levels.
- Each level introduces a new puzzle mechanic.
- Multiple possible solutions for certain levels.
- Collectible hidden golden origami stars.
- Unlockable character skins and environments.

WORLDS:

1. Paper Forest
2. Frozen Origami
3. The Forgotten City
4. Floating Islands
5. The Cosmic Paper World

VISUAL STYLE:
Beautiful stylized 3D graphics, realistic paper textures, dynamic shadows, satisfying folding animations, atmospheric lighting and polished environments.

USER INTERFACE:
Minimalist mobile interface with Play, Level Selection, Settings and Skins.

IMPORTANT:
Make the folding mechanic the central feature of the game. The player must physically manipulate the geometry of the level, not simply activate predefined bridges or teleport objects.

Create a fully playable prototype with a main menu, tutorial, at least 10 playable levels, restart functionality, level progression, sound effects and mobile-friendly controls.

Prioritize smooth performance on Android devices.Don't try to build all 100 levels right away. First, create 3 fully functional levels and focus on perfecting the folding mechanic. Make sure the controls feel intuitive, the animations are smooth, and the puzzles are genuinely fun. If the core mechanic is enjoyable, you'll have a strong foundation for a successful game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')

    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')

### Game logic architecture

`class Game`:
Properties:
- renderer, scene, camera, clock, raycaster, pointer
- state: 'menu' | 'level' | 'paused' | 'complete'
- levelIndex, levelData
- worldGroup, panels[], paperMeshes[], staticMeshes[]
- player object {group, pos: Vector3, groundY, vy, facing, ...}
- stars[], exitGroup, enemy[], props
- fold: {panel, stationary, pivot, axis:Vector3, pivotPoint:Vector3, side:number, angle, target, state}, pendingCrease
- input: joystick vector, keys, pointer states
- menu scene separate.

Methods:
- init(): renderer, resize, build menu scene, animation loop.
- loadLevel(index, {instant}): clear world group, build from data, frame camera, set player, reset state, UI callbacks.
- buildWorld(level): create sheets (panels), static boxes, exit, stars, props, enemies, decor, particles.
- update(dt): menu drift or game update; fold animation; player movement; enemies; props animation; particles; camera; renderer.
- Input handlers.
- UI callbacks via `this.on = {}`.

To manage UI, `main.js` handles DOM and calls game methods. Game emits `emit(event, data)` with a simple object. Events: `levelready`, `star`, `complete`, `trapped`, `foldstart`, `foldchange`, `foldend`, `crease`, `hint`, `playerfall`, `toast`, `theme`.

```
splitPanel(panel, axis, coord, movingSign) {
  const movingCells = cellsOnSide(panel.cells, axis, coord, movingSign);
  const stayCells = ...
  if moving empty return null
  const origGroup = panel.group
  const makePanel = (cells) => {
    const p = { cells, bounds:..., y: origY? group pos, group: new THREE.Group(), ...}
    p.group.position.copy(origGroup.position); p.group.quaternion.copy(origGroup.quaternion);
    p.group.scale.copy(origGroup.scale);
    const mesh = createPanelMesh(p, theme); p.group.add(mesh); worldGroup.add(p.group);
    this.panels.push(p); this.groundMeshes.push(mesh)
    return p
  }
  const stay = makePanel(stayCells)
  const move = makePanel(movingCells)
  // reparent attachments
  for (const att of [...panel.attachments]) {
    const val = axis==='x' ? att.position.x : att.position.z;
    const goes = movingSign>0 ? val >= coord : val < coord;
    (goes?move.group:stay.group).attach(att);
    (goes?move:stay).attachments.push(att);
  }
  // remove orig
  worldGroup.remove(origGroup); dispose mesh
  // remove panel from arrays
  // pivot:
  const pivotY = origGroup.position.y (sheet mid)
  const pivotPos = axis==='x' ? new Vector3(coord, pivotY, 0) : new Vector3(0, pivotY, coord)
  const pivot = new THREE.Group(); pivot.position.copy(pivotPos); worldGroup.add(pivot);
  pivot.attach(move.group); // preserves world
  // axis vector world:
  const axisVec = axis==='x' ? (0,0,1) : (1,0,0); // because x=const line along Z
  // sign: rotation around axis by signed angle lifts moving side.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile 3D paper-folding puzzle adventure game called **THE LAST FOLD**, prioritizing a polished and genuinely fun folding mechanic.

## Requirements
- Paper world; swipe to create fold line, drag one side over the other; objects/enemies/characters move with the folded paper; overlapping surfaces create bridges/shortcuts; incorrect folds can trap the player.
- Third-person isometric 3D camera, smooth touchscreen controls, main menu, tutorial, restart, level progression, sound effects, mobile-friendly UI.
- Main menu with Play, Level Selection, Settings, Skins.
- Collectible golden origami stars; unlockable character skins and environments.
- 5 worlds: Paper Forest, Frozen Origami, The Forgotten City, Floating Islands, Cosmic Paper World.
- Stylized 3D graphics, paper textures, dynamic shadows, atmospheric lighting.
- Prioritize smooth Android performance.
- User explicitly narrowed initial scope: first make 3 fully functional levels and perfect the folding mechanic; do not build all 100 levels yet. Earlier text also mentions at least 10 playable levels.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; state assumptions briefly at finish.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport max 1280px wide), read only latest.

## Decisions
- Built with static HTML/CSS/vanilla ES modules + locally vendored Three.js `r170` (no Vite).
- Levels use integer grid paper cells; free fold lines are axis-aligned and snapped to cell boundaries.
- Fold mechanic supports angles 0/45/90/135/180°, with drag-up gesture and snap on release.
- Each sheet can be folded once; multiple independent sheets allow multi-fold levels.
- Plan created for **10 levels** across all 5 worlds, despite the 3-level priority, to satisfy the earlier "at least 10" requirement; first levels are tutorial-focused.
- Character, stars, and exits keep upright orientation while their anchors transform with folded paper; decorations rotate physically with the paper.
- Player can ride folded paper; trap detection auto-restarts.
- Exposed debug API planned via `window.__lastfold` for testing.
- Procedural audio, no external assets except font files and Three.js.

## Work State

### Completed
- Scaffolded static project structure: `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/`, `vendor/`, `assets/`, `screenshots/`.
- Downloaded/vendored Three.js `0.170.0` to `vendor/three.module.js`.
- Downloaded font assets: `assets/fraunces.woff2`, `assets/nunito.woff2`.
- Wrote complete UI markup with screens: menu, level select, skins, settings, game HUD, pause, complete, how-to-play, loading, toast.
- Wrote full design system CSS (`css/style.css`).
- Wrote `js/themes.js` with 5 themes, 4 palettes, 5 skins.
- Wrote `js/audio.js` procedural sound/music engine.
- Wrote `js/paper.js` procedural textures, merged paper geometry, props, player origami fox, stars, exit seals, islands, clouds, particles, lighting.
- Wrote `js/levels.js` with 10 level definitions, sheet/platform helpers, hints, stars, enemies, decor data.
- Wrote `js/game.js` engine with menu diorama, level build, fold splitting/animation, player movement/collision, stars, exit, enemies, traps, hints, camera framing, debug helpers.

### Active
- `js/main.js` has **not been created yet**.
- Game has not been started, tested, or screenshotted.
- No validation of level solvability or folding UX yet.

### Blocked
- None, but likely runtime bugs need fixing after first browser test.

## Next Move
1. Fix known bugs before running:
   - `js/paper.js` `makeCreaseLine`: dash positions/orientation are wrong for axis `x`/`z`; use per-instance quaternion `Qx(-90°) * Qy(axis==='x'?90°:0)`, base dash plane `0.26 × 0.06`, positions along Z for axis `x`, X for axis `z`.
   - `js/game.js` `showHint` must set `guide.userData.axis = hint.axis` for `_updateHint` glint animation.
   - `js/game.js` `_disposeScene` disposes `scene.background` but sky textures may be reused; verify no crash.
   - Check `js/paper.js` `createPaperBox` cloned material/texture disposal.
2. Create `js/main.js`: save/load localStorage, screen routing, menu/levels/skins/settings wiring, joystick, tutorial banner, HUD, pause/complete overlays, skins/palettes, `window.__lastfold` debug API.
3. Start static server on port 3002 (tmux per repo conventions) and test with Playwright.
4. Capture menu and level-1 screenshots; fix layout/visual issues.
5. Simulate level 1 crease/fold/walk; verify exit reachable and fold controls intuitive.
6. Validate/fix levels 2–10 with debug folds and movement; adjust coordinates/hints.
7. Test mobile viewport 390×844 and desktop; check console errors, performance.
8. Add final README/project notes if needed and report assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: core engine just written; most likely source of runtime bugs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/paper.js`: crease-line bug and all visual builders.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/levels.js`: 10 level coordinate definitions; needs solvability validation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: UI structure/import map; missing `js/main.js`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: complete UI styling; needs screenshot-driven polish.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: procedural sound engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/themes.js`: theme/skin/palette data.

- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; git repo, all new game files currently uncommitted.
- No `package.json`; static server path via `index.html`.
- Serve on port `3002`; use preinstalled `playwright-cli` / Playwright at `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright`.

- `startLevel` calls `_disposeLevel`, rebuilds scene/player, then `_computeBounds`/`_frameLevel`.
- Player uses orthographic camera, ground raycasting against `groundMeshes`; supports `_groundAt`, `_tryMove`, `_beginRide`.

- Planned save key: `lastfold_save_v1` (not yet implemented).
- `start.sh` expects `RUNTIME_DIR`; simpler to run `python3 -m http.server 3002` or `PORT=3002 bash start.sh` in tmux.
- Screenshot requirement: save small `.jpg` files at max 1280px viewport width; read only the latest screenshot.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile 3D paper-folding puzzle adventure game called **THE LAST FOLD**, prioritizing a polished and genuinely fun folding mechanic.

## Requirements
- Paper world; swipe to create fold line, drag one side over the other; objects/enemies/characters move with folded paper; overlapping surfaces create bridges/shortcuts; incorrect folds can trap the player.
- Third-person isometric 3D camera, smooth touchscreen controls, main menu, tutorial, restart, level progression, sound effects, mobile-friendly UI.
- Main menu with Play, Level Selection, Settings, Skins.
- Collectible golden origami stars; unlockable character skins and environments.
- 5 worlds: Paper Forest, Frozen Origami, The Forgotten City, Floating Islands, Cosmic Paper World.
- Stylized 3D graphics, paper textures, dynamic shadows, atmospheric lighting.
- Prioritize smooth Android performance.
- User narrowed initial scope: first make 3 fully functional levels and perfect the folding mechanic; do not build all 100 levels yet. Earlier text also mentions at least 10 playable levels.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; state assumptions briefly at finish.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport max 1280px wide), read only latest.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/vanilla ES modules + locally vendored Three.js `r170` (no Vite).
- Levels use integer grid paper cells; free fold lines are axis-aligned and snapped to cell boundaries.
- Fold mechanic supports angles 0/45/90/135/180°, with drag-up gesture and snap on release.
- Each sheet can be folded once; multiple independent sheets allow multi-fold levels.
- Plan created for **10 levels** across all 5 worlds, despite the 3-level priority, to satisfy the earlier "at least 10" requirement; first levels are tutorial-focused.
- Character, stars, and exits keep upright orientation while their anchors transform with folded paper; decorations rotate physically with the paper.
- Player can ride folded paper; trap detection auto-restarts.
- Debug API exposed via `window.__lastfold` for testing.
- Procedural audio, no external assets except font files and Three.js.
- Save key `lastfold_save_v1` implemented; star totals (sum of level bests) double as skin/palette unlock thresholds.
- Responsive camera: desktop uses diagonal isometric direction; portrait uses `(1.08, 1.18, 0.56)` so long level axis runs up-screen.

## Work State

### Completed
- Full static project scaffold, UI markup, design-system CSS, 5 themes/4 palettes/5 skins.
- `js/audio.js` procedural sound/music engine.
- `js/paper.js` procedural textures, merged panel geometry, props, paper fox, stars, exit seals, islands, clouds, particles, lighting, corrected crease-dash orientation.
- `js/levels.js` 10 level definitions, hints, stars, enemies, decor; levels 6/8/9/10 coordinates reworked for solvability.
- `js/game.js` engine with menu diorama, level build, fold splitting/animation, player movement/collision, stars, exit, enemies, traps, hints, camera framing.
- `js/main.js` created: save/load, screen/overlay routing, menu/levels/skins/settings wiring, joystick, tutorial banner, HUD, pause/complete overlays, palette/skin unlocking, debug API, pause on tab hide.
- Menu redesigned into editorial split layout on desktop (left title/actions, right diorama); mobile haze backdrop; menu camera target shifted.
- Lighting contrast increased (hemi 0.82, sun 2.85, exposure 1.0); forest palette deepened; player scaled 1.12.
- Camera framing/zoom improved, especially mobile portrait.
- Crease/hint line visibility increased.
- Tall decorations suppressed on moving fold flaps; bridge sheets no longer decorated.
- Live server on `http://localhost:3002` (tmux session `lastfold`).
- Playwright browser opened via session `lastfold`; needed symlinks `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243 -> chromium-1248` and `chromium_headless_shell-1243 -> chromium_headless_shell-1248`.

"Create a complete mobile 3D puzzle adventure game called THE LAST FOLD.

CORE CONCEPT:
The entire game world is made of paper. The player controls a small character who must reach the exit of each level by physically folding the world using touchscreen gestures.

MAIN GAME MECHANICS:

- Swipe across the screen to create a fold line.
- Drag one side of the paper world over the other.
- Objects, platforms, enemies and characters move together with the folded paper.
- Overlapping surfaces can create bridges, shortcuts and new paths.
- Some objects can only be reached by flipping or folding the world.
- Incorrect folds can create obstacles or trap the player.

GAMEPLAY:

- Third-person isometric 3D camera.
- Smooth touchscreen controls.
- 100 progressively challenging levels.
- Each level introduces a new puzzle mechanic.
- Multiple possible solutions for certain levels.
- Collectible hidden golden origami stars.
- Unlockable character skins and environments.

WORLDS:

1. Paper Forest
2. Frozen Origami
3. The Forgotten City
4. Floating Islands
5. The Cosmic Paper World

VISUAL STYLE:
Beautiful stylized 3D graphics, realistic paper textures, dynamic shadows, satisfying folding animations, atmospheric lighting and polished environments.

USER INTERFACE:
Minimalist mobile interface with Play, Level Selection, Settings and Skins.

IMPORTANT:
Make the folding mechanic the central feature of the game. The player must physically manipulate the geometry of the level, not simply activate predefined bridges or teleport objects.

Create a fully playable prototype with a main menu, tutorial, at least 10 playable levels, restart functionality, level progression, sound effects and mobile-friendly controls.

Prioritize smooth performance on Android devices.Don't try to build all 100 levels right away. First, create 3 fully functional levels and focus on perfecting the folding mechanic. Make sure the controls feel intuitive, the animations are smooth, and the puzzles are genuinely fun. If the core mechanic is enjoyable, you'll have a strong foundation for a successful game.

---
